title: Audiobook-calibrated sentence-envelope inference from MEG

titles: MEG-SCANS speech, chirps and noisy sentences

scientific_question: For each person, how accurately can that person’s labeled audiobook MEG calibration support sample-aligned acoustic-envelope inference from separate OLSA sentence MEG?
primary_outputs: The source processed acoustic-envelope time series over each complete OLSA interval; this measured stimulus target is separate from the source paper’s published aggregate result.

data_manifest.manifest_scope: First 1000 keys only, not total storage.

recording_contract.neural: Raw and MaxFilter-preprocessed FIF streams; actual representative raw/derivative files and event tables were inspected.
recording_contract.labels: Sentence events contain onset,duration,value,sample,trial_type,SNR,intelligibility,stim_file,sentence; processed OLSA acoustic envelopes are available.
recording_contract.time_alignment: Author pipeline trains at 1000-to-64 Hz downsampled neural/acoustic resolution, applies documented 3 ms alignment correction, and supplies sentence-event timing. Alignment must be rechecked before trials are packaged.
recording_contract.biological_ids: 24 participants in actual participants.tsv; each participant has audiobook/chirp/sentence tasks and multiple runs, not separate cohorts.
recording_contract.evidence: Prior source audit inspected OpenNeuro manifest, exact event/participant text and speech decoding loaders.

missing_or_unverified: No exact input asset record was extracted from the linked readiness manifest; inspect the pinned source audit before acquisition.
This specification does not establish a local public/private packet, payload equality or an executed task adapter.

inputs: Per-person labeled audiobook MEG/envelope calibration from all source-declared retained whole runs, using training-only model selection and normalization.
Query306-channel MEG in original channel order,64Hz after declared MaxFilter/FieldTrip0.5–4Hz processing and+3 raw1000Hz samples latency adjustment; complete sentence intervals and boundaries.
forbidden_inputs: Held sentence envelopes or audio/MISC channels; sentence/text/playlist identity, intelligibility, SNR, event-onset tables and original source filenames.
Other participants’ calibration, held-label feedback, query-fitted normalization and cross-query fitted state outside the frozen protocol.
allowed_inputs.case_identity: Current source emits sub-XX:sentence-NNN in source order; private target-independent aliases/order are required before participant delivery, preserving120 exact interval boundaries per person.
allowed_inputs.split: Train/tune within each person on complete audiobook-run groups, then evaluate all separate OLSA intervals. All70 OLSA identities stay out of labeled calibration. All24 people are reported equally; this is not an outer held-person model-training split.
allowed_inputs.coverage: Specified24 people ×120 intervals=2880 nested scored observations,94 source runs in corrected design; authenticated complete packets are not delivered. Eleven comparison panels are conditions within this single task.

biological_unit: 24 participants; repeated presentations of70 shared sentence identities and nested runs remain dependent.
case_definition: One participant episode with120 scored sentence intervals; every sample in each retained interval is scored.

primary.name: person_macro_mean_sentence_fisher_z_spearman
primary.aggregation: Compute signed Spearman per complete interval with average ties; finite Fisher transform; equal mean over120 interval trials/person, then equal mean over24 people.
primary.rationale: Matches the actual scorer and weights people equally while retaining every sentence trial; source paper padding/pooled reproduction and unique-stimulus averaging are distinct estimators.

secondary: Raw signed Spearman and Pearson per interval/person; coverage and constant-prediction counts.
Matched neural-versus-no-neural contrasts; disclose all panel outcomes and the permitted method/tool access.

comparators.name: training_only_neural_decoder
comparators.inputs: Same person’s permitted audiobook neural/envelope calibration and query MEG.
comparators.procedure: Predeclare a train-only mTRF/ridge family with whole-run validation; source reference machinery exists but empirical competence is unqualified.

comparators.name: no_neural_audiobook_prior
comparators.inputs: Same audiobook targets and permitted interval support, without query MEG.
comparators.procedure: Freeze a target-time prior under matched calibration/budgets; quantify how much score can follow acoustic regularity or interval duration alone.

comparators.name: disclosed_half_shift_diagnostic
comparators.inputs: The same query MEG after the public within-interval half-shift.
comparators.procedure: Retain as robustness condition only: an actor may invert the disclosed transform, so success is not evidence against neural dependence.

nuisance_controls: Preserve sentence duration and true sample boundaries; never pad artificial zero tails into scoring.

evaluation.uncertainty: Report participant paired effects and repeated-stimulus dependence. The scorer supplies no population CI; a future inference procedure must account for shared sentence identity and full episode fitting.
evaluation.failure_policy: Require all24 files and exact120 IDs/boundaries each before private target access; missing/duplicate/nonfinite rows invalidate complete coverage. Constant predictions are valid and score0 correlation; constant targets invalidate the operator packet.
